title: 2 weeks I didn’t know how to code / New Workshops update
author: 2nd_breakfastt
selftext:
and I still don’t lmao! but check out the progress of the workshops in my game Valdmark | Medieval Sandbox

Every trade now has its house: workshops, production chains and hands-on crafting

This update is all about making a settlement feel like it actually works

Check out the demo https://ynotved.itch.io/valdmark

# Real workshop buildings

Your villagers now build a proper house for each trade instead of dropping benches into cottages: smithy, carpenter's shop, mason's yard, weaver's house, herbalist's hut, brewhouse, bakehouse, windmill and a watermill with its wheel in the stream. They go up in stages, can be turned four ways, and the worker lives there too

# You can see the work happen

Iron glows on the anvil and stretches into a blade, the quench steams, logs get sawn down into planks, cloth grows on the loom, flour sacks fill at the mill, and the finished goods stack up in each workshop's store. Walls drop when you look inside

# Everything feeds the next trade

Ore to ingots to swords on a guard's hip. Logs to planks to barrels. Grain to flour to bread on the table

# Or work it by hand

Any station can open a short hands-on minigame: heat, hammer and quench a sword at the anvil, steer the saw along the line, judge the bread in the oven, keep rhythm at the loom, and more. Play well and you get better quality (a flawless round can even beat the workshop's limit), or just let your villagers do it. Mini games are prototype versions for now and will be polished next update

**How AI was used**  
Claude (Anthropic's AI) writes the Godot code, builds the 3D models in code and filmed and edited this trailer from in-game footage. I use ChatGPT to brainstorm ideas and make concept and reference art

comments.author: TashLai
comments.body: Wait 2 weeks for all this or just some last piece of work?

replies.author: 2nd_breakfastt
replies.body: Less than that actually! Started building Valdmark 9 days ago on Nov 15th

replies.author: 2nd_breakfastt
replies.body:
My biggest takeaway from that video: is to have multiple agents talking with each other and bouncing ideas back and forth between them

For example, after I’ve told my ai agents the exact process of how my games being built (what engines /programs you’re using), I brainstorm an idea with GPT 6. I then have Opus 5.5 analyze and revise the response and go back and forth until it’s where I want it 

I then tell GPT 6 to give me a technical breakdown that I give Claude to apply to the game

Reference images are must haves (screenshots with arrows, gameplay clips, etc) to get the visuals to where you want them

Have GPT generate you reference images, then ask GPT to give you technical instructions for Claude to apply it. So instead of the prompt being “make my game look more visual pleasing and have a more medieval look”. Instead, GPT will expand on that prompt, and give Claude the exact directions to implement in your game

replies.body: thankfully I have taken enough game design courses, this is just a normal task without needing to watch a video on something I have learned already.  Should help others.  I am going to check out this video also.

replies.author: TashLai
replies.body: But how did you manage the visuals in so little time? I mean i take it you had 2d version so it's basically you handle TWO different kinds of visuals in 9 days?!

replies.author: 2nd_breakfastt
replies.body:
An awful sleep schedule and caffeine lmao. After work I spend a gross amount of hours into early morning tweaking/adjusting/brainstorming/playtesting building reference images, reference sheets etc

First thing I did was build an art bible (colors you want, camera angles, art style, perspectives etc)

I had a pretty good idea of what I wanted the game to look like, so I made references, then built an art bible around those references

Big part of my game is that instead of art assets being directly imported into the game, my reference images are being used to procedurally draw all of the art through code
